full_judgment: 3. It was the contention of the petitioner that he had performed his part by depositing 25% of the price offered as down payment, the respondents were under a legal obligation to hand over possession of the Hotel to him and that having not been done so the respondents, failed to perform their duties as required by law. The petitioner also filed Supplementary Affidavit before the High Court Division stated that the building in which the hotel was located became abandoned property was also held by the High Court Division in its judgment dated 3rd March 1980 passed in writ petition No. 1485 of 1974. In the Supplementary Affidavit it was asserted by the petitioner that the owner Md. Buksh acquired the property in 1948 and that the property in question was never within the periphery of Khulna Boro Bazar and the same was never made khas as per provision of section 20 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and that fact of making the land and building in question khas was not published in the Gazette dated 14.3.1962 and that the owner Md. Buksh did not receive any compensation nor the Government took over possession and that the property in question was never under the control and management of the Government. The respondent Khulna City Corporation filed an Affidavit-in-opposition stating, inter alia, that the property in question situated within the property of Khulna Hat and Bazar and was acquired by the Government under section 3(1) and 3(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. Upon initiating a proceeding being Misc. Case No. 1 of 1961-62 under section 20(2a) of the Act and that compensation Assessment Roll in respect of the property in question and other properties of the Khulna Bazar was made final and notification to that effect was made on 15th March, 1962 and that the said notification was published in Dhaka Gazette, Extraordinary dated 21th March 1962, that possession of the property was taken over by the Circle Officer (Revenue) Khulna Sadar and that the property was managed by the Government. Since the property in question was a property under the control of the Government the same did not assume the character of an abandoned property; that the person, by name Md. Buksh, who was running M/S. Afgania Hotel in portion of the building was absent after liberation of the country. The property in question being the property of the Government as could not be an abandoned property and that the property although mistakenly was treated as abandoned property for some-time managed through the Ministry of Industries and that at one stage notified for sale and the petitioner dropped tender to purchase the property but fact remained that the land and the building being the property owned by the Government was never an abandoned property and that at best as the Hotel that was owned by Mr. Buksh a non-local, could be abandoned business or Commercial concern, the petitioner was not entitled to claim the property in any respect and on any legal basis. The property being under the control of the Government could not be an abandoned property and Investment Board was not competent to sell the same as abandoned property. M/s. Afgania Hotel was located in a chandina property within the periphery of Khulna Boro Bazar appertaining C.S. Khatian Nos. 1254 an 1255 corresponding to S.A. Khatian No. 1 and the Plot Nos. (C.S.) 3288, 3289 and 3290 corresponding S.A. Plot Nos. 3288, 3289 and 3290 in Mouza Baniakhamar, Police Station Khulna, District Khulna. The Deputy Commissioner, Khulna on 17.4.84 handed over the property to the Khulna City Corporation and that the fact of handing over of possession to the City Corporation and that the fact of handing over of possession to the City Corporation was communicated to the Member Secretary, Sub-Committee for Disinvestment after taking over of possession.
